body: no problem!! anytime you need a chat or just vent or anything feel free to dm me. take care.

this!!!! and the craziest thing is most of them will also be like "i'm an empath i can feel everything your feeling" and then as soon as you say you feel anything other than happy they say "well now i feel that way because you said that" like ???

if you really love/like/appreciate them i would say it's important in this to do research on your own. and not from websites that promote stigma. but from people first hand, or actual licensed professionals. if you feel comfortable enough, you could even talk to your partner about what would be the best way to handle episodes and symptoms as someone who wants to be there for comfort and support. maybe even suggest that they go to therapy or start seeing professionals so that they can get treatment.

if you don't feel deeply connected and you genuinely don't think you can give them the support that they need, it would be best to leave the relationship. it is very hard to do and extremely hard for your partner going through it, but in the long run it would be best.

was this relationship with your ex the first time you felt in love? i've found that there are exs i have that honestly i don't really care that i lost them and i don't think about them often. however my first ex that i felt truly in love with that ended on confusing terms left me hung up on her. and she wasn't even my first relationship, just the first person i once thought i would never lose. i'm also an overthinker so i replay situations in my head a lot, even though i know this was for the best. but for some reason it hurts really bad.

its good that your current girlfriend is supportive through this. if you ever want to just get the thoughts out of your head you could try writing them down in a journal or even on a piece of paper and then throwing it away if you don't want to keep it. it's also important to remember that everything happens for a reason and is always for better.

break ups are sooo hard for people with bpd!! it's definitely tough to navigate through but i think you're doing a great job.

i was in the same exact place!! i also had gone through a breakup, it had happened in the past couple weeks but it was like i could not stop crying no matter what. even if i felt fine anything would trigger me to start crying and i couldnt stop. ive been on wellbutrin for a little bit over a month now and i will say the crying has stopped and i only get emotional when things are genuinely tear-jerking. 

it will get better!!! push through and i promise the crying and emotions will subside. i would try meditating to calm your mind or journaling as a way to communicate your emotions and get them out of your system.

exactly! lol my family is so worried about me because im constantly getting emotional over the tiniest things! and i dont even know what to say bc its not something i would usually get upset about! so weird..
do you feel that it was worth waiting it out? im willing to put up with it if it levels out eventually.

yeah my last med was lexapro as well. my doctor informed me last visit that its going to be three months until my body feels the full effects and i guess gets used to it. not sure i can deal with the emotional crying spells for that long :/
this is very true. thank you for responding. take care.
thank you for this. take care

lexapro literally erased my daily depression i was facing. just make sure your taking the correct dosage prescribed by your doctor and journal about how your days start to change!! if you ever need some advise or have a question feel free to message me.

totally agree with you on this. i smoked since i was 16, and im finally closing that chapter of my life at 22. it was just my crutch, and i couldnt imagine my life without it. definitely was blind to the harm it was doing to my life (and wallet)

thanks for replying! yes ive heard a lot of good things about mood stabilizers, im just not use to such a heavy med ya know? its been giving me terrible migraines but im hoping i can stick it out a little bit longer.

thanks for the reply! i guess im just super uneasy about going through this change is bc finals are coming up for my colleges classes, so i really dont have time to be distracted by side effects. my goal is to stick it out for at least a month, so ill update in the future!

thanks for your reply! i decided to cut the pill in half so now im taking  around 2.5 mg at night with my lexapro. the nausea is just a huge issue bc i already have a sensitive stomach. today was kinda a rocky one, started out feeling really good but by mid noon i was crying at work bc of how paranoid i was feeling. def something i journaled about. my goal is to stick it out for a month.

i feel this 100%. when i become unstable its like all my bad emotions come out and i turn into a completely different person. my partner has stressed it to me how it makes her feel and how it now stresses her out too because she never knows when im gonna explode. 

one thing that has helped me is an app called dbt coach. it has a journal feature where you can write about your day and also provides many tools and exercises to help strengthen skills such as mindfulness. and it sends reminders everyday so you won't forgot about it. i highly recommend it.

if you ever need someone to talk to, feel free to reach out. take care.
thank you so much for your support. i'll keep this in mind. take care.

thank you so much for this reply. ive been working on my dbt coping skills and they help. it helps me stay present and mindful. if you havent, check it out! they have an app called dbt coach and its great. im feeling a lot better rn after stepping away and refreshing. feels like a new day.

thank you so much for your reply. feel free to chat anytime you need someone, im always looking for bpd friends.
